questions.prompt: What do the four WCAG principles (POUR) stand for?
questions.explanation: WCAG organises all success criteria under Perceivable, Operable, Understandable and Robust.

questions.prompt: Which attribute gives an informative image a text alternative?
questions.explanation: `alt` provides the text alternative. `title` is not reliably announced, `aria-hidden` hides content, and `role` sets semantics.

questions.prompt: A decorative image should have an empty alt attribute (alt="") so screen readers skip it.
questions.explanation: Empty alt marks the image as decorative. Omitting alt entirely makes some screen readers read the file name.

questions.prompt: Under WCAG 2.2 AA, what is the minimum contrast ratio for large text (at least 18pt, or 14pt bold)?
questions.explanation: Large text needs 3:1 at AA. Normal text needs 4.5:1; 7:1 is the AAA level for normal text.

questions.prompt: Which were added as new success criteria in WCAG 2.2? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Focus Not Obscured, Target Size (Minimum) and Accessible Authentication are among the WCAG 2.2 additions. 1.1.1 has existed since WCAG 2.0.

questions.prompt: An automated scanner reports zero issues on a checkout page. What should you conclude?
options: Only that the automatically detectable issues are absent; keyboard, screen-reader and content checks are still needed
The page conforms to WCAG AA
questions.explanation: Automated tools catch a subset of issues (missing alt, contrast, some ARIA errors). Many criteria need human judgement.

questions.prompt: A form passes a scanner, but screen-reader users cannot tell what the field is for. What is wrong?
options: The placeholder is not a reliable label and disappears on typing; the visible text is not programmatically associated. Use <label for="email">
questions.explanation: Placeholders are not a substitute for labels: they vanish, often fail contrast, and may not be announced. A `<label>` linked by `for`/`id` names the field.

questions.prompt: A custom dropdown built from <div>s works with a mouse but not with the keyboard, and NVDA announces it as "clickable". What is the best recommendation?
options: Use a native <select> if possible; otherwise implement the ARIA combobox/listbox pattern with full keyboard support and states
questions.explanation: Native elements come with semantics and keyboard behaviour for free. A custom widget needs correct roles, states and keyboard handling; an aria-label alone does not make it operable.

coding.title: WCAG contrast ratio
coding.prompt:
Write `contrast(hex1, hex2)` that returns the WCAG contrast ratio of two `#rrggbb` colours, rounded to 2 decimals. Relative luminance: for each channel c in 0..1, linear = c/12.92 if c <= 0.04045 else ((c+0.055)/1.055)**2.4; L = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B. Ratio = (L1 + 0.05)/(L2 + 0.05) with L1 the lighter.

Example: `contrast('#000000', '#ffffff')` returns `21.0`.
coding.explanation: This is the WCAG 2.x definition. Taking the max/min makes the order of arguments irrelevant. #767676 on white is about 4.54:1, the classic 'just passes AA' grey.
hints: Convert each pair of hex digits with `int(x, 16) / 255`.
Apply the linearisation per channel before weighting.
Put the lighter luminance on top.

coding.title: Pass or fail at AA
coding.prompt:
Write `passes_aa(ratio, size_pt, bold)` returning True if the contrast ratio meets WCAG 2.2 AA: large text (size >= 18pt, or >= 14pt and bold) needs 3.0; other text needs 4.5.

Example: `passes_aa(3.2, 14, True)` returns `True`; `passes_aa(3.2, 14, False)` returns `False`.
coding.explanation: Large text is easier to read at lower contrast, so WCAG relaxes the threshold. Note the ratio is compared without rounding up: 4.49 fails.
hints: Pick the threshold with a conditional expression.

tests.name: Bold 14pt is large
tests.code: assert passes_aa(3.2, 14, True) is True and passes_aa(3.2, 14, False) is False

tests.name: Normal text thresholds
tests.code: assert passes_aa(4.5, 12, False) is True and passes_aa(4.49, 12, False) is False

tests.name: 18pt is large
tests.code: assert passes_aa(3.0, 18, False) is True and passes_aa(2.99, 24, True) is False
